# Fixture design
Provide a pure, side-effect-free Python validation library. No third-party dependencies. Preserve caller input. Task 1.1 implements a scalar contract; task 1.2 composes it for batches. No network, logging, persistence, CLI application, or other features.
# Tasks
- [ ] 1.1 Implement and test validate_positive_integer.
- [ ] 1.2 Implement and test validate_batch, depending on 1.1.
# Requirements and scenarios
R1 / AC1: validate_positive_integer(value) accepts built-in int (type(value) is int) greater than zero and returns the same value. bool, floats, strings, None and other types raise TypeError. Zero and negative ints raise ValueError. Test normal, boundary and error paths.
R2 / AC2: validate_batch(values) accepts a built-in list only, else TypeError. It returns a NEW list of validated integers in input order, without modifying input. Empty list returns a new empty list. Every element uses the exact R1 contract. First invalid element raises the same TypeError or ValueError; no partial result is returned. Test empty, valid, invalid element, input type and input preservation.
# Design
Use validate_positive_integer from validate_batch; no mutation or partial output. Exceptions propagate. Existing placeholder bodies return None and must be implemented with TDD.
# Proposal
Validate scalar and batch input consistently with observable exceptions. Deliver only local Python implementation and tests.
